title: Tariff Fatigue And Trump’s Next Move
gist: Gavekal argues markets are numb to Trump's proposed Section 301 'structural excess capacity' tariffs on 14 partners (Goldman: US effective rate 7.8%→9.2%), but trading partners — notably China and Brazil — are threatening retaliation; the tariffs are built to be legally sturdier than the invalidated reciprocal regime and are leverage for concessions from China, Vietnam and India, while the EU's 15% cap averts a US-EU war. (Teaser excerpt only.)

insights.claim: Markets barely reacted to the USTR's proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners because tariffs are largely priced in and the proposed increases for most partners are modest.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Tariff headlines have low market beta now — fade tariff-driven selloffs unless retaliation escalates.

insights.claim: Goldman Sachs estimates the proposed Section 301 tariffs would raise the overall US tariff rate from 7.8% to 9.2%.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Modest ~1.4pt effective-rate increase — limited incremental inflation/growth impact.

insights.claim: The Section 301 tariffs, based on an eight-month USTR investigation into 'structural excess capacity,' are designed to be more legally robust than Trump's invalidated reciprocal tariff regime.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Lower legal-reversal risk means these tariffs are more durable than prior ones — price them as sticky.
insights.locator: The proposed tariffs, released by the Office

insights.claim: The White House sees the new Section 301 tariffs as leverage to extract further trade concessions from China, Vietnam and India; China is the principal target, followed by Vietnam, India and other Asian emerging economies.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Asian EM exporters face renewed tariff/negotiation risk; watch concession headlines from Hanoi and New Delhi.
insights.locator: But the White House sees the tariffs as leverage

insights.claim: Although markets shrugged off the tariff proposal, China and Brazil both raised the prospect of retaliation, so trading partners cannot afford the same tariff fatigue investors show.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Retaliation risk is under-priced relative to market complacency.

insights.claim: Washington intends to respect tariff ceilings in bilateral deals, capping the EU's tariff at 15% (with an option to raise to 20%), which should avert a renewed US-EU tariff war.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Reduces tail risk for EU exporters; the 20% option is the residual risk to watch.
insights.locator: Washington intends to respect tariff ceilings
